title: The Cipher of Geneva
premise: Rosalind Winterbourne, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 447, has spent five years buried in bureaucratic anonymity—until a burner phone rings with the voice of her brother, who supposedly died in that crash. The call pulls her into a conspiracy in which the airline's parent company has been faking disaster victims to smuggle assets and witnesses across borders, and Rosalind's own investigation file is the key to exposing it. Hunted by the company's fixers and betrayed by the mentor who taught her every rule she follows, she must trade the one secret worth killing for—the true passenger manifest proving her family was murdered, not lost—to bring the network down. In the end she chooses truth over survival, publishing the manifest at devastating personal cost and walking away with nothing but her name.
about_author: Marguerite Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who left the field after a decade of investigating accidents no one wanted explained. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Jura mountains, where the fog rolls in like a redaction.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Five years after losing her family on Flight 447, Rosalind works crash investigations under a deliberately dull name, hiding inside procedure. While archiving old files she finds an anomaly in the passenger manifest—a seat assignment that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: grief recast as dread; the past is not finished with her.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A phone with no service history appears in her mailbox and rings: her brother Daniel's voice, alive, whispering that he never boarded—that row twelve was emptied before takeoff. The line cuts when someone tries her door. Emotional beat: vertigo of hope; everything she mourned may be a lie.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. She pulls the official wreckage report and discovers pages quietly amended since her last review—her own annotations erased. Her supervisor, Marcus Hale, warns her off with genuine fear in his eyes. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting; the rules she trusted are weapons pointed at her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me to Look
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Rosalind and Elias Voss, her retired mentor. Voss admits he helped falsify the original manifest to protect witnesses being smuggled out under dead passengers' names—including Daniel. He begs her to stop digging. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth; the father figure becomes the first betrayer.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Following Daniel's coordinates to a Geneva safehouse, she finds it sterilized except for a photograph of their family with one face circled—and a fixer waiting for her. She escapes by using investigation protocol as tradecraft, but now they know she knows. Emotional beat: hunter becomes hunted.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Decoding her brother's hidden notes, she reconstructs the true Flight 447 list: eleven living people declared dead, including a whistleblower carrying evidence against the company's board. The company didn't kill her family—they erased them from existence to erase him. Emotional beat: fury crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind and Marcus. Marcus confesses he's been reporting on her for years to keep her safe, and offers to get her out of the country if she burns the manifest. Daniel resurfaces, insisting some truths will only get more people erased. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit; two loves, two impossible choices.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. She confronts dying Voss, who gives her the final piece—the board's authorization order—and asks her forgiveness with his last breath. Company agents raid the hospice; she barely escapes with the document. Emotional beat: grief layered on grief; absolution refused and given at once.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Cornered in the airport's freight terminal, Rosalind negotiates with the fixer: the manifest in exchange for Daniel walking free. She hands it over—then reveals she broadcast encrypted copies to three journalists the moment she entered the building. Emotional beat: climax; she trades the secret worth killing for and wins by refusing to hoard it.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. The story breaks; the board falls; Daniel disappears into a new life, sending only a postcard. Rosalind signs her real name to the published investigation, ending her five years of invisibility—at the cost of the career, safety, and family she can never recover. Emotional beat: resolution; truth survived her, and that is enough.
